enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 18–30 determine when property in unascertained goods passes by appropriation, regulate delivery of specific goods into deliverable state, approval or sale-or-return transactions and reservation of disposal, allocate prima facie risk, and prescribe statutory exceptions to the nemo dat rule.

Definition: This group determines when ownership and risk pass and when a non-owner can give a buyer a valid title under the statutory exceptions.

Ingredients:
1. Identify whether goods are specific, ascertained or unascertained.
2. Determine whether property has passed under the parties’ intention and statutory rules.
3. For unascertained goods, identify unconditional appropriation.
4. Determine when risk follows property subject to the Act.
5. If title comes from a non-owner, identify the precise statutory exception in sections 27–30.
examples: A buyer receives goods on approval and retains them beyond the agreed or reasonable period without rejection; the sale-or-return rules in section 24 determine when property may pass.
